operations.description:
Cast a helpfulness vote on a review.

This operation allows customers to indicate that they found a review helpful. Each customer can cast only one helpfulness vote per review. The system tracks the vote timestamp and maintains referential integrity with both the review and customer accounts.

When a customer casts a helpfulness vote, the system:
- Creates a new record linking the customer to the review
- Records the timestamp of the vote
- Updates the review's helpfulness metrics

Security considerations:
- Only authenticated customers can cast helpfulness votes
- Each customer can vote only once per review
- Customers cannot vote on their own reviews
- Deleted reviews cannot receive helpfulness votes

This operation supports the platform's quality assessment system by enabling the community to identify valuable reviews.

operations.description:
Retrieve historical snapshots of a specific refund request.

This operation allows sellers who fulfilled the associated order item, and administrators, to view complete snapshots of the refund request at different points in its lifecycle. Snapshots are immutable records that capture the request state, reason, status, and timestamps at specific moments (original submission and when the seller responds with approval or rejection).

## Access Control
- **Sellers**: Can only view snapshots for refund requests directly associated with order items they fulfilled
- **Administrators**: Can view snapshots for any refund request for dispute resolution
- **Customers**: Cannot view refund request snapshots (this is seller/admin functionality only)

## Snapshot Content
Each snapshot includes:
- The original reason text at time of snapshot
- The request status (pending, approved, or rejected) at that time
- Timestamp of when the snapshot was created
- The response timestamp if the seller responded at that snapshot
- Complete snapshot data JSON that preserves all relevant request information

## Use Case
Sellers use this endpoint to review the complete history of refund requests for items they fulfilled, particularly during dispute resolution. Administrators use it to investigate refund disputes and verify that proper procedures were followed.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query the ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots table filtered by refund_request_id. Join with ecommerce_mall_refund_requests to verify the seller owns the fulfillment for the associated order item (unless admin). Return snapshots sorted by created_at in descending order (newest first) with pagination support. Include all snapshot fields: snapshot_type, reason, status, responded_at, created_at, updated_at. Apply soft delete filtering if applicable.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of refund request snapshots with complete state history

operations.description:
Submit a cancellation request for a paid order item.

This operation allows customers to request cancellation of a specific order item they have purchased. Each order item can have only one cancellation request (one-to-one relationship). The request must include a reason for cancellation and will be processed by the seller who fulfilled the order.

When a customer submits a cancellation request, the system will:
- Validate that the order item exists and belongs to the customer
- Ensure no existing cancellation request exists for this order item
- Create a cancellation request record with status "pending"
- Associate the request with the appropriate seller for resolution

The cancellation request will progress through a status workflow:
1. "pending" — Initial state when created
2. "approved" or "rejected" — Final states when seller responds

When the seller responds to a cancellation request (approving or rejecting), the system will:
- Update the request status and record the response timestamp in responded_at
- Create a snapshot record in ecommerce_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots for audit
- If approved, restore inventory for the cancelled item
- Notify the customer of the decision

If an attempt is made to create a cancellation request for an order item that already has an active request or is not in a cancellable status, the system will reject the request with an appropriate error.

For sellers, the system provides endpoints to approve or reject cancellation requests using PATCH operations on specific request IDs. These operations will update the request status and trigger the appropriate business logic including stock restoration for approved cancellations.

This operation is part of the comprehensive cancellation workflow that ensures proper handling of customer cancellation requests while maintaining audit trails through snapshot records.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new cancellation request for an order item.

1. Parse request body to extract order_item_id, reason, and status
2. Validate that order_item_id references an existing order item
3. Verify that the order item belongs to the current customer (from authentication)
4. Check that no cancellation request already exists for this order_item_id (enforce unique constraint)
5. Create a new cancellation request record with the provided data
6. Set status to "pending" for new requests
7. Generate unique ID for the request
8. Record created_at and updated_at timestamps
9. Return the created cancellation request with all fields

Business logic validation:
- Order item must be in a cancellable status
- Customer must be the owner of the order item
- Only one cancellation request per order item allowed
- Seller will be determined from the order item's seller relationship

After successful creation, the system will notify the seller and prepare the request for resolution.

responseBody.description: The created cancellation request with all fields including auto-generated timestamps

requestBody.description: Cancellation request details including order item ID, reason, and status

Create a new refund request for a delivered order item.

This endpoint allows customers to initiate a refund request for items that have been delivered. Customers can request refunds within 7 days of the item being delivered, and must provide a text reason explaining why they want the refund.

The system will verify that the specified order item has status 'delivered', check that no pending refund request already exists for this item, and ensure the delivery was within the 7-day window. If any validation fails, the operation will be rejected with an appropriate error message.

This operation is part of the customer service workflow for handling post-delivery issues and product dissatisfaction. Once created, the refund request will appear in the seller's pending actions dashboard for approval or rejection.

Process refund request creation for a delivered order item.

1. Extract order_item_id and reason from request body
2. Verify order item exists and customer owns it
3. Check order item status is 'delivered' (reject if not)
4. Verify delivery date is within 7 days (reject if older)
5. Check no pending refund request exists for this item (reject if duplicate)
6. Create refund_request record with status='pending', customer_id, seller_id from order item
7. Create initial snapshot with reason, status='pending', timestamps
8. Return the created refund request

Transaction: Create refund request and snapshot atomically.
Validation: Apply all business rules before persistence.

operations.description:
Retrieve the audit history of refund request snapshots.

This operation returns a chronological list of all snapshots created for a specific refund request. Each snapshot captures the complete state of the refund request at the time it was created, including the reason text, status (pending/approved/rejected), response timestamp, and snapshot data. Snapshots are immutable and permanently preserved as part of the audit trail, allowing customers, sellers, and administrators to review the history of a refund request.

## Security and Permissions

- Customer: Can view snapshots for refund requests they initiated
- Seller: Can view snapshots for refund requests they are involved in
- Administrator: Can view all refund request snapshots for dispute resolution

## Business Rules

- Snapshots are created automatically when the refund request is created or when a status change occurs (approval/rejection)
- Snapshots are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted
- All snapshots are permanently preserved regardless of request deletion
- Each snapshot includes the exact reason, status, and timestamps at that moment in time

## Use Cases

- Customer reviewing their refund request history before approval
- Seller verifying the reason and status changes during their review process
- Administrator investigating a dispute by examining the complete history of changes

Apply database-level filtering on refund_request_id to ensure data isolation.
Validate that requesting actor has permission to view this refund request's snapshots based on their role (customer, seller, or admin).

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific administrator request.

This endpoint fetches the complete details of an administrator request using its unique identifier. The request contains information about a user's application for administrative privileges including the requesting user's account details, the reason text provided during application, the current status of the request (pending, approved, or rejected), and the timeline of all status changes.

The system maintains an immutable record of each admin request, preserving the original state at creation time. Status changes are logged separately while the original request content remains unchanged, providing an audit trail for compliance and administrative review.

Only super administrators have access to view administrator requests. Regular administrators and regular users cannot access this endpoint.

The operation supports retrieving requests at any stage of their lifecycle, including:
- Pending requests awaiting super administrator review
- Approved requests that resulted in admin role assignment
- Rejected requests with documented rejection reasons

Related operations:
- `GET /admin-requests/pending` to list all pending requests (super admin only)
- `POST /admin-requests` to submit a new admin request (authenticated users)
- `PATCH /admin-requests/{id}/approve` to approve a pending request (super admin only)
- `PATCH /admin-requests/{id}/reject` to reject a pending request (super admin only)

**Validation Rules:**
- The admin request ID must exist in the system
- Only super administrators can access this endpoint
- Access attempts by unauthorized users are logged for security audit

Approve or reject a pending administrator role application.

This operation allows super administrators to review and decide on pending admin role requests submitted by customers or sellers. When approving, it creates an admin role record for the requesting user. When rejecting, it records the rejection reason for audit purposes.

Security considerations:

- Only users with super administrator grade role can perform this operation
- Users cannot approve or reject their own requests (self-demotion prevention)
- All actions are logged for security audit
- Rejection requires providing a reason text

The operation updates the admin request status and performs the appropriate side effect:
- Approval creates an admin role entry with the requested grade
- Rejection records the rejection reason without creating an admin role

Process admin request approval or rejection by super administrator.
1. Verify user has super-admin grade role (permission check)
2. Load admin request by ID and validate status is 'pending'
3. For approval: create admin role record with user_id
4. For rejection: store rejection_reason and set status
5. Update admin_request record with super_admin_id and responded_at
6. Commit transaction and log action in admin_action_logs

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific administrator role assignment.

This operation fetches a single administrator role entry by its unique identifier, providing complete details about the role assignment including the administrator's grade level (regular or super), assignment timestamps, and role hierarchy information. This endpoint is essential for privilege verification and audit trail requirements.

The response includes the administrator's assigned grade, which determines their access level to platform management operations. Super administrators have elevated privileges for managing other administrators, while regular administrators have standard platform management capabilities.

This operation supports the platform's role-based access control system by providing precise role assignment information for security verification. The timestamps in the response enable comprehensive audit tracking of when each role grade was assigned and last updated.

## Security Considerations:

- Access to this endpoint is restricted to authenticated administrators
- Regular administrators can only access their own role assignments
- Super administrators have access to view any administrator's role assignment
- Role assignment details are logged for security audit purposes

## Related Operations:

- **GET /admin-roles**: List all administrator role assignments
- **PATCH /admin-roles/{adminRoleId}**: Update administrator role grade
- **GET /admin/users/{id}/role**: Get user's current role assignment

## Error Handling:

- Returns 404 Not Found if the admin role ID does not exist
- Returns 403 Forbidden if the requesting administrator lacks permission to view the role
- Returns 401 Unauthorized if not authenticated as an administrator

operations.description:
Submit an administrator role access request.

This endpoint allows users to formally request administrator privileges. The request is stored in the system and requires review and approval by a super administrator before any role changes take effect.

## Authorization

Any authenticated user can submit an admin request. However, the request will only be processed by super administrators who have the authority to approve or reject administrator access requests.

## Request Flow

1. User submits admin request with justification
2. System validates user is not already an admin (regular or super)
3. System stores request with pending status
4. Super administrators can later approve or reject the request
5. Upon approval, admin role is created; upon rejection, request is marked rejected

## Related Operations

- GET /admin/requests/pending - List pending requests (super admin only)
- PATCH /admin/requests/:id/approve - Approve admin request (super admin only)
- PATCH /admin/requests/:id/reject - Reject admin request (super admin only)
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new admin request record in the ecommerce_mall_admin_requests table.
1. Verify the requesting user is not already an admin (check their role is customer or seller)
2. Create admin_request record with the user_id from authentication, status = 'pending', and provided reason
3. Return the created admin_request with timestamps
4. Do NOT create admin_role automatically - admin_role is only created upon approval of this request

responseBody.description: Created admin request with pending status

requestBody.description: Admin request details including justification

operations.description:
Update administrator role grade.

This operation allows super administrators to modify the grade (regular|super) of an administrator role assignment. It enables the platform's role hierarchy management by permitting privilege escalation or降格 for administrators.

**Authorization**: Only users with super administrator grade can perform this operation. Regular administrators cannot modify any admin roles, including their own.

**Self-Demotion Prevention**: Super administrators cannot demote themselves to regular administrator. The system will reject such attempts.

**Audit Trail**: All grade changes are logged in the admin_action_logs table with timestamp, actor information, and the grade change details.

**Error Conditions**:
- Insufficient privilege: Returns error if non-super-admin attempts the operation
- Self-demotion prevention: Returns error if super admin attempts to demote themselves
- Invalid grade: Returns error if invalid grade value is provided
- Role not found: Returns error if the specified admin role ID does not exist

**Related Operations**:
- GET /admin-roles: Retrieve administrator role information
- POST /admin-requests: Request administrator access
- PATCH /admin-requests/:id/approve: Approve admin requests

**Business Rules**:
- Only super administrators can modify admin role grades
- Self-demotion (super admin demoting themselves) is blocked
- Grade history is preserved through admin_action_logs
- All changes are immediately effective for permission evaluation
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update ecommerce_mall_admin_roles table grade field by adminRoleId.

1. Verify requesting user has super admin grade
2. Load target admin role by adminRoleId

Insert new scheduled task definition into ecommerce_mall_scheduled_tasks table.
Validate cron_expression format and concurrent_policy values.
Set next_execution_at based on cron expression and timezone.
Initialize success_count and failure_count to 0.
Set status to 'pending' on creation.
Return created task with all computed fields.

responseBody.description: Created scheduled task definition with all configuration and metadata

requestBody.description: Scheduled task configuration including cron scheduling, execution policy, timeout, and retry settings

operations.description:
Update an existing scheduled task configuration.

This operation allows administrators to modify the configuration of a scheduled task including its name, description, cron expression for scheduling, timezone settings, execution timeout, retry configuration, concurrent execution policy, and active status.

The update preserves all historical execution data and performance metrics associated with the task while allowing modification of the scheduling and execution parameters.

**Key Capabilities:**

- Modify task identification fields (name, description)
- Update scheduling configuration (cron expression, timezone)
- Adjust execution parameters (timeout, max retries, retry delay)
- Change concurrent execution policy
- Enable or disable the task

**Security Considerations:**

- Requires administrative privileges for authentication
- Audit logging captures the modification for compliance
- Role-based access control ensures only authorized users can modify critical scheduled operations
- Version control preserves previous configurations for rollback capability

**Related Operations:**

- `GET /scheduled-tasks/{taskId}` retrieves current task details
- `GET /scheduled-tasks` lists all scheduled tasks
- `POST /scheduled-tasks` creates a new scheduled task
- `DELETE /scheduled-tasks/{taskId}` removes the scheduled task
- `PATCH /scheduled-tasks/{taskId}/execute` triggers manual execution

**Error Handling:**

- Returns 404 if task with specified ID does not exist
- Returns 400 if cron expression format is invalid
- Returns 409 if task status is incompatible with update (e.g., running)
- Returns 403 if user lacks administrative permissions

**Timestamp Fields:**

- updated_at: Automatically set to current timestamp on successful update
- The task's execution history and metrics remain unchanged by configuration updates
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update scheduled task configuration while preserving execution history.

1. Retrieve the scheduled task by ID, verifying existence
2. Validate user has administrative privileges
3. Apply updates to modifiable fields only:
   - name, description
   - cron_expression, timezone
   - timeout_seconds, max_retries, retry_delay_seconds
   - concurrent_policy
   - is_active
4. Validate cron expression format if provided
5. Update updated_at timestamp to current time
6. Save changes and return updated task
7. Log the modification for audit trail

Return 404 if task not found, 403 if unauthorized, 400 for invalid cron format.

responseBody.description: Updated scheduled task with current configuration

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the scheduled task to update
parameters.name: taskId

requestBody.description: Configuration fields to update for the scheduled task

operations.description:
Delete a scheduled task definition and permanently remove it from the system.

This operation permanently deletes the scheduled task definition including its metadata, scheduling configuration, and execution history tracking. Once deleted, the task will no longer execute according to its cron schedule, and all future scheduled executions are cancelled.

**Important:** This operation permanently removes the task definition but preserves historical execution records for audit and compliance purposes. The actual execution logs and historical data are retained in the system for reporting and troubleshooting, but the task definition itself is permanently removed.

**Security Considerations:**
- Only administrators with appropriate privileges can delete scheduled tasks
- Deletion is irreversible and immediately stops all future task executions
- System administrators should verify task dependencies before deletion
- Audit logs record the deletion event including who performed it and when

**Common Use Cases:**
- Removing obsolete scheduled tasks after system upgrades
- Cleaning up test or development tasks from production
- Disabling scheduled operations that are no longer needed
- Removing misconfigured tasks before re-creating with correct settings

**Relationship to Related Operations:**
- Use GET /scheduled-tasks/{taskId} to verify task details before deletion
- Use PATCH /scheduled-tasks/{taskId} to disable a task instead of deleting it
- Use GET /scheduled-tasks to list all active tasks and identify candidates for deletion

**Error Scenarios:**
- 404 Not Found: Task with the specified ID does not exist
- 403 Forbidden: User lacks administrative privileges
- 409 Conflict: Task is currently running and cannot be deleted (if such constraint exists)
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Delete a scheduled task by its unique identifier. The operation permanently removes the task definition from the ecommerce_mall_scheduled_tasks table including all configuration fields. Historical execution records in job_queues referencing this task should be preserved for audit purposes. The task will be immediately removed from the scheduler queue and will not execute again. Return the deleted task details including all metadata fields for confirmation.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the scheduled task to delete
parameters.name: taskId

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of rate limit tracking records.

This operation provides comprehensive monitoring capabilities for API rate limiting policies. Administrators can filter rate limit tracking records by IP address, user ID, time window, and blocking status to identify abuse patterns, troubleshoot rate limiting issues, and review rate limit policy effectiveness.

Features include time-based filtering to review historical rate limit events, IP-based filtering to track specific client behavior, and blocked status filtering to monitor currently restricted clients. Supports pagination for efficient data browsing and sorting by time window start for chronological analysis.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_rate_limit_trackings table with pagination and filtering.
Apply filters on ip, user_id, window_start time range, window_end time range, and blocked status.
Join with customer, seller, and admin tables via user_id for user information if needed.
Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Sort by window_start descending by default.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of rate limit tracking summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific rate limit tracking record.

This operation fetches the complete rate limit tracking record identified by its UUID. The record includes the client IP address, user identifier (if authenticated), request count within the current time window, window timestamps, and blocking status.

Administrators use this endpoint to investigate rate limiting events, verify current rate limit status of specific IP addresses or users, and audit rate limiting policy enforcement. The detailed information helps identify patterns of abuse and verify that rate limiting is functioning correctly.

Security considerations: This operation requires administrative privileges to prevent unauthorized access to rate limiting data, which could be used to identify targets for rate limiting attacks or bypass rate limiting systems.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_rate_limit_trackings table by primary key id (UUID).
Return the complete rate limit tracking record including ip, user_id, request_count, window_start, window_end, blocked, and blocked_until fields.
Include null handling for optional user_id and blocked_until fields.
Nojoins required - single table lookup.

responseBody.description: Rate limit tracking record with complete details

parameters.description: Target rate limit tracking record's UUID identifier
parameters.name: trackingId

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of API access logs.

This operation provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for API access logs, enabling system administrators and developers to identify and investigate specific API requests. The logs capture detailed information about each API request including client IP address, request URL, HTTP method, authentication status, response latency, and error information.

The operation supports multiple filter criteria including IP address, URL path, HTTP method, response status code, latency thresholds, error message presence, and date ranges. This enables efficient debugging, security auditing, and performance monitoring of the API system.

Each log entry includes the request and response body hashes for integrity verification, along with timestamps for tracking and chronological analysis of API activity.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_api_logs table with pagination and filtering.
Apply filters on IP address, URL path, HTTP method, response status, latency range, error message presence, and date range (created_at_range).
Join with customer/seller tables if authentication info is available.
Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets and support sorting by created_at timestamp in ascending or descending order.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of API access log summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for API access logs

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific API request log.

This operation fetches comprehensive details about a particular API request captured in the system's logging infrastructure. Each log entry captures detailed information about API requests including client IP address, request URL, HTTP method, authentication status, response latency, and error information when applicable.

The API access logs are designed for audit trails, debugging, monitoring, and compliance purposes. These logs provide visibility into system activity and can be used to investigate issues, track usage patterns, and maintain security audits.

Access to these logs is restricted to authorized administrators and system users with appropriate permissions to view audit data.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_api_logs table by primary key ID.
Return complete log entry including all fields: ip, href, method, user_agent, authorization_header, request_body_hash, response_status, response_body_hash, latency_ms, error_message, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.
Implement soft-delete logic to exclude records with non-null deleted_at timestamps.
Return 404 Not Found for soft-deleted or non-existent log entries.
Include join with user table if user association exists for enhanced context.

responseBody.description: Complete API access log entry with all details

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of administrative action logs.

This operation provides comprehensive access to the platform's audit trail, allowing administrators to search and filter administrative actions performed on the platform. It supports detailed filtering by action type, date range, target entity, and administrator, enabling thorough compliance monitoring and operational auditing.

The operation returns sorted results (default: newest first) with configurable pagination, supporting large-scale audit data retrieval. Response includes essential information about each administrative action including the admin who performed it, action type, target entity, and description.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_admin_action_logs table with pagination and filtering.
Apply search filters on action_type, created_at date range, target_id, and admin_id.
Join with ecommerce_mall_admins for admin information if requested.
Default sort by created_at DESC (newest first). Return paginated results with configurable page size.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of admin action log summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific admin action log entry for audit trail inspection.

This operation provides detailed visibility into administrator actions performed on the platform, supporting compliance, security auditing, and operational accountability. Each log entry captures the complete context of an administrative action including who performed it, when, what action was taken, and the affected entity.

The audit log preserves an immutable record of all administrative operations performed by super administrators and regular admins, including seller registration approvals, product deletions, user bans, order overrides, and administrative category management.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_admin_action_logs table by logId to retrieve the specific admin action log entry.
Return the complete audit record including timestamp, actor information, action type, target entity, and action details.
Ensure the logId is properly validated as a UUID format before querying.

responseBody.description: Admin action log entry with complete audit details

parameters.description: Target admin action log's UUID identifier
parameters.name: logId

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of notification queue entries.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities including filtering by notification type (email or in-app), status (pending, sent, failed, delivered), date ranges, and error conditions. It supports comprehensive notification tracking and management workflows.

Admin actors can view all notification queues, while regular users can only access their own notifications. The system preserves notification history for audit trails and compliance requirements.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_notification_queues table with pagination and filtering.
Apply search filters on type, status, user_id, and timestamp ranges.
Support filtering by delivery status (pending|sent|failed|delivered).
Filter by error messages for failed notifications.
Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets.
Enforce user-level data isolation for non-admin actors.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of notification queue summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific notification by its unique identifier.

This operation fetches detailed information about a system notification including its type (email or in-app), content, delivery status, and any error messages if delivery failed. Notifications are used to communicate important updates to users such as order confirmations, shipping notifications, and system alerts.

The operation provides visibility into the notification delivery history and current status, allowing users to track whether their notifications have been successfully delivered or if any issues occurred during delivery.

This operation accesses the `ecommerce_mall_notification_queues` table which stores system-generated notification records with delivery tracking information. The table contains fields for notification type, content, delivery status, and error handling information.

### Security and Authorization
This operation is restricted to admin users only. Regular users cannot directly access notification queue records as these are system-generated logs for internal monitoring purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_notification_queues table by id field to retrieve a single notification record.
Return complete notification details including type, content, status, and error information.
Ensure notification exists and belongs to the requesting user (unless admin access).
Return 404 if notification not found.

responseBody.description: Notification details including content, status, and delivery information

operations.description:
Retrieve filtered and paginated integration logs from external API interactions.

This operation provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for integration logs that track interactions with external services including payment gateways, shipping carriers, and other third-party APIs. It enables debugging, monitoring, and auditing of external service communications.

The operation supports multiple filtering dimensions including service type (payment, shipping, external_api), status (success|failure|timeout), date ranges, request/response durations, and error conditions. This allows technical teams to investigate specific integration issues, monitor system health, and analyze external service performance.

Response includes essential log information optimized for list displays, with full log details available through individual log retrieval operations if needed.

Security: Access is restricted to admin actors only. Regular customers and sellers cannot access integration logs as they contain sensitive technical implementation details about external service configurations.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters

responseBody.description: Paginated list of integration log summaries

operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_integration_logs table with pagination and filtering.

Apply filters on service_type (payment|shipping|external_api), status (success|failure|timeout), request_date (date range), error_message (partial match), and duration_ms (min/max).

Join with related tables if additional context is needed (e.g., linking to orders for payment logs).

Return paginated results with essential log information.

Implement cursor-based pagination for large result sets.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific external API integration log entry.

This operation fetches the complete record of an external API integration call, including payment gateway transactions, shipping carrier interactions, and other third-party service communications. The log contains comprehensive request and response details for debugging, audit trail, and monitoring purposes.

This operation requires appropriate administrative permissions to access integration logs. Regular customers and sellers do not have permission to view integration logs.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the ecommerce_mall_integration_logs table by the provided logId to retrieve a single integration log entry. Return all fields including integration_type, api_endpoint, request/response headers and bodies, response status, error_message, and duration_ms. Verify user has administrative permissions before returning the log data.

responseBody.description: Detailed integration log record

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete category hierarchy for browsing and product discovery.

This operation returns all top-level categories with their direct subcategories (one level deep) in a hierarchical structure. Customers use this endpoint to browse product categories when shopping, while administrators can view the category structure for oversight purposes.

The response includes category names, descriptions, and their parent-child relationships. Top-level categories (where parentId is null) are returned at the root level, and each top-level category includes its subcategories if any exist. Subcategories cannot have further children due to the one-level nesting restriction.

Security considerations:
- This is a public read-only endpoint accessible to all users
- No authentication required for browsing categories
- Administrators have additional write access to create/update/delete categories
- The system enforces one-level nesting depth (subcategories cannot have children)

Related operations:
- POST /categories: Create a new category (admin only)
- PATCH /categories/{id}: Update an existing category (admin only)
- DELETE /categories/{id}: Delete a category (admin only)
- GET /categories/{id}: Get details for a specific category
- GET /products: Search and filter products (uses categories for filtering)
operations.name: get
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_categories table to retrieve hierarchical category structure.
Load all top-level categories (where parent_category_id is null).
For each top-level category, load its direct subcategories (where parent_category_id matches the category's id).
Apply one-level nesting constraint: subcategories must not have children.
Sort top-level categories alphabetically by name.
Sort subcategories alphabetically by name within each parent.
Return hierarchical structure with categories and their nested subcategories.

responseBody.description: Complete category hierarchy with nested subcategories

operations.description:
Retrieve seller dashboard statistics and performance metrics.

This operation provides essential seller analytics including total active product count, pending cancellation and refund request counts, order item summaries with sales volume and revenue statistics. The data is filtered to only include products and orders belonging to the authenticated seller.

The operation supports filtering by order item status to get breakdowns for paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, and refunded items. Response includes aggregated metrics optimized for dashboard display and summary views.
operations.name: stats
operations.specification:
Query seller's active products, pending cancellation requests, pending refund requests, and order item statistics.
Join ecommerce_mall_products (seller_id, deleted_at IS NULL), ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests (seller_id, status='pending'), ecommerce_mall_refund_requests (seller_id, status='pending'), and ecommerce_mall_order_items (seller_id, optional item_status filter).
Aggregate: count of active products, count of pending cancellation requests, count of pending refund requests, count of order items per status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), sum of item totals by status.
Apply seller context from authenticated user's seller profile.
Return summary statistics without individual records.

responseBody.description: Seller dashboard statistics summary

requestBody.description: Request parameters for filtering and pagination

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated seller dashboard statistics for product and order performance.

This operation provides a comprehensive overview of seller business performance including product inventory counts, pending request monitoring, and sales analytics. The dashboard statistics are calculated from active (non-deleted) products and all-time order data for products owned by the authenticated seller.

Security Considerations:
- Only accessible by authenticated sellers
- Data is scoped to products owned by the authenticated seller
- Excludes products from suspended sellers in aggregated metrics
- Does not expose customer or order-level detail

Related Operations:
- GET /sellers/dashboard/order-items retrieves filtered order items list with pagination for detailed viewing
- GET /products provides product listing for inventory management
- PATCH /order-items/:itemId/approve-cancel handles individual cancellation approvals
- PATCH /order-items/:itemId/approve-refund handles individual refund approvals
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Calculate seller dashboard statistics by querying the ecommerce_mall_products and ecommerce_mall_order_items tables.
1. Count active products: COUNT(*) WHERE sellerId matches authenticated seller AND deletedAt IS NULL
2. Count pending cancellation requests: COUNT(*) WHERE sellerId matches authenticated seller AND status = 'pending'
3. Count pending refund requests: COUNT(*) WHERE sellerId matches authenticated seller AND status = 'pending'
4. Total order items sold: COUNT(*) WHERE sellerId matches authenticated seller
5. Product performance: GROUP BY productId SUM(quantity) as total_units, SUM(productPrice * quantity) as total_revenue
6. Apply optional filters from request body (date range, category filters)
7. Return aggregated statistics as IEcommerceMallDashboard

responseBody.description: Seller dashboard statistics summary

requestBody.description: Dashboard statistics query parameters and filters

operations.description:
Validate the customer's shopping cart for checkout eligibility.

This operation performs comprehensive validation of all cart items to determine their eligibility for checkout. It checks each item's variant availability, stock quantity, seller status, and other business rules that must pass before an order can be created.

The validation examines:
- Whether each cart item's product variant still exists (not deleted)
- Whether each variant has sufficient stock for the requested quantity
- Whether each variant's seller is active and not suspended
- Whether all items belong to the same seller (cross-seller cart limitation)

The response provides detailed information about each item's validation status, including specific reasons for any failures. Items that fail validation are marked as unavailable and cannot be included in the checkout process.

After successful validation, the customer can proceed with checkout. If any items fail validation, the customer must remove or modify those items before attempting checkout again.
operations.name: patch
operations.specification:
Validate all cart items for the authenticated customer.
Query cart_items table joined with product_variants and sellers tables.
For each cart item, check:
1. Variant exists (deleted_at is null)
2. Variant stock_quantity >= cart_item.quantity
3. Seller is not suspended (is_suspended = false)
4. All items belong to same seller (cross-seller validation)
Return validation results with availability status and failure reasons for each item.

responseBody.description: Cart validation results with availability status for each item

requestBody.description: Validation options and filter criteria

operations.description:
Retrieve inventory transaction history for a specific product variant.

This operation provides sellers with detailed audit trail of all stock level changes for their product variants. The history includes restocks, order fulfillment, inventory adjustments, cancellation reversals, and refund reversals with precise timestamps and quantitative changes.

Access is restricted to sellers who own the parent product. The system enforces strict data isolation to prevent viewing inventory history for variants belonging to other sellers.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query inventory_records table filtered by variant_id and product ownership.
Apply date range filtering if provided in request body.
Apply reason code filtering if provided (restock|order|adjustment|cancel|refund).
Calculate current stock level by summing all records.
Return paginated results sorted by created_at descending.
Enforce seller ownership verification before querying.

responseBody.description: Paginated inventory transaction history

requestBody.description: Inventory history query criteria

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated review analytics and statistics for products.

This endpoint provides statistical summaries and analytics about customer reviews across products in the system. It calculates aggregate metrics such as average ratings, total review counts, rating distributions (1-5 star breakdowns), and time-based trends.

The analytics data is automatically calculated by the system based on review data and does not require manual input or management. This endpoint supports filtering by product, time range, and other criteria to generate targeted analytics reports.

Administrators and sellers can use these analytics to understand customer sentiment, identify product quality issues, and track review patterns over time. The analytics are derived from the ecommerce_mall_reviews table and its relationships with ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots for historical review data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_reviews table with analytics aggregations.
Calculate average ratings using AVG() with ROUND() to one decimal place.
Count total reviews using COUNT(), excluding deleted reviews.
Calculate rating distribution using conditional aggregation for each star rating (1-5).
Support filtering by product_id, time range (created_at range), and rating range.
Support pagination with offset/limit or cursor-based pagination.
Include seller_id filtering for seller-specific analytics.
Return paginated analytics summary with calculated statistics.

responseBody.description: Paginated analytics summary for reviews

requestBody.description: Analytics query criteria and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated review analytics and statistics for products.

This endpoint provides statistical summaries and analytics about customer reviews across products in the system. It calculates aggregate metrics such as average ratings, total review counts, rating distributions (1-5 star breakdowns), and time-based trends.

The analytics data is automatically calculated by the system based on review data. The system manages this analytics data as a derived metric from the ecommerce_mall_reviews table, and it does not require manual input or management.

This endpoint supports filtering by product, time range, and other criteria to generate targeted analytics reports. Administrators and sellers can use these analytics to understand customer sentiment, identify product quality issues, and track review patterns over time.

The analytics are derived from the ecommerce_mall_reviews table, and the query excludes soft-deleted reviews (where deleted_at IS NULL) to ensure accurate statistics. For detailed review edit history, administrators and sellers can access the ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots table separately.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_reviews table with analytics aggregations.
Calculate average ratings using AVG() with ROUND() to one decimal place.
Count total reviews using COUNT(), excluding deleted reviews.
Calculate rating distribution using conditional aggregation for each star rating (1-5).
Support filtering by product_id, time range (created_at range), and rating range.

Return paginated analytics summary with calculated statistics.

operations.description:
Retrieve seller dashboard statistics for product and order performance tracking.

This endpoint provides sellers with a comprehensive overview of their store performance including total active products count, pending cancellation request count, pending refund request count, and total order items sold. These statistics are essential for sellers to monitor their business metrics at a glance.

Access control ensures that only authenticated sellers can retrieve their dashboard statistics. If a seller account is suspended, the endpoint returns an appropriate error response. The statistics are calculated from the seller's perspective, counting only their own products and order items.

The dashboard statistics are updated in real-time as sellers process orders, respond to cancellation and refund requests, or modify their product inventory. This provides immediate visibility into their store performance.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query seller dashboard statistics from the database. Calculate total products count (excluding deleted), pending cancellation request count, pending refund request count, and total order items sold. All counts are filtered by the authenticated seller's ID. Return the statistics as a summary DTO.

responseBody.description: Seller dashboard statistics including total products, pending cancellation requests, pending refund requests, and total order items sold.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of pending administrator role requests for super administrator review.

This operation provides super administrators with access to all pending admin role applications, allowing them to review applicant information, the reason for requesting administrative privileges, and the request timestamp.

Super administrators can view all pending requests regardless of when they were submitted. Regular administrators do not have access to this endpoint and will receive an access denied error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_admin_requests table where status = 'pending'.
Include related applicant (customer/seller) information and reason text.
Return paginated results ordered by creation timestamp (newest first).
Only super administrators can access this endpoint - regular admins receive 403 Forbidden.
No soft delete column - permanently deleted requests not included.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of pending admin request summaries

requestBody.description: Pagination and sorting parameters

operations.description:
Approve or reject a pending seller registration request.

This operation allows administrators to review seller registration requests and make a decision to approve or reject the seller's application. When an administrator approves a seller registration, the seller's account becomes active and they can begin using the platform to manage products and process orders. When rejecting a seller registration, the administrator must provide a rejection reason explaining why the application was denied.

Only administrators with appropriate permissions can access this endpoint. Regular administrators and super administrators can approve or reject seller registrations. The system enforces that rejection reasons are provided when rejecting a registration request, ensuring sellers receive clear feedback on why their application was denied.

The operation updates the approval status field of the seller registration request, sets the responded_at timestamp to the current time, and stores the rejection reason if the request is being rejected. After approval, the associated seller account transitions to an active state and can begin using platform features.

Related operations:
- GET /admin/sellers/pending - List pending seller approvals to identify registrations requiring review
- PATCH /admin/sellers/:id/suspend - Suspend an already approved seller account if policy violations occur
- GET /admin/sellers/:id/orders - View orders from an approved seller for oversight purposes
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
Update ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations table to set approval_status and responded_at.
Validate that the incoming administrator has regular or super admin role.
Validate that the seller registration exists and has approval_status = 'pending'.
When approval_status = 'approved': set approval_status to 'approved', null rejection_reason, set responded_at.
When approval_status = 'rejected': require rejection_reason field to be non-empty string, set approval_status to 'rejected', set responded_at.
Update responded_at to current timestamp.
Return updated registration request with all fields.

responseBody.description: Updated seller registration request with new approval status

requestBody.description: Approval decision and optional rejection reason

operations.description:
Reject a seller registration request with a specified reason.

This operation allows administrators to formally reject a seller registration request after reviewing the provided information. When a registration is rejected, the system records the rejection reason and timestamp, allowing the seller to understand why their application was denied and potentially resubmit a new registration.

The rejection reason must be provided by the administrator and stored permanently in the system for audit purposes. This operation is only available to users with administrator role and is typically called after reviewing the seller's registration details.

After rejection, the seller's account remains in a pending state until they submit a new registration request with corrected or updated information. The original registration record is preserved in the database for compliance and audit tracking, but the seller's registration status will reflect the rejection.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification:
Update ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations table to set approval_status to 'rejected', store rejection_reason from request body, and set responded_at to current timestamp.

1. Find registration by seller user_id (ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations.user_id)
2. Verify registration exists and approval_status is currently 'pending'
3. Update approval_status to 'rejected'
4. Set rejection_reason from request body
5. Set responded_at to current timestamp
6. Return updated registration record

responseBody.description: Updated seller registration with rejection details

requestBody.description: Rejection request with reason and optional response timestamp

operations.description:
Permanently ban a user (customer or seller) with specified reason and optional expiration time.

This operation allows authorized administrators to restrict user access to the platform by creating a permanent ban record. When a user is banned, the system immediately terminates all active sessions and prevents future login attempts while preserving all historical data (orders, products, reviews) for audit and compliance purposes.

The ban can be temporary (with unban_at timestamp) or permanent (unban_at = null). The system enforces ownership-based access control, ensuring only administrators with sufficient privileges can perform this operation. Users cannot ban themselves, and attempts to ban suspended sellers or banned users are rejected.

This endpoint supports polymorphic user targeting through user_type field ("customer" or "seller") combined with user_id reference, allowing comprehensive platform-wide user management from a single endpoint.
operations.name: create

requestBody.description: Ban request containing user identifier, type, ban duration, and reason

responseBody.description: Created ban record with all metadata including ban ID, timestamps, and user reference

operations.specification:
Create a new user ban record in ecommerce_mall_user_bans table.
1. Validate admin authentication and verify admin has sufficient privileges
2. Verify target user exists in either customers or sellers table based on user_type
3. Reject if target user is already banned (is_active = true)
4. Reject if banning a suspended seller (check seller_suspensions table)
5. Create ban record with current timestamp as banned_at
6. If unban_at provided, store it; otherwise set to null for permanent ban
7. Set is_active = true
8. Trigger session termination for all active sessions in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions or ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions tables
9. Return created ban record with all fields

operations.description:
Remove active ban status from a user.

This operation removes the active status from a user ban record, effectively unbanning the user. It updates the is_active field to false and records the unban timestamp.

Only administrators with either regular or super grade can perform this operation. The system verifies the requesting user's admin role grade before allowing the unban action.

The operation preserves the complete ban history record for audit and compliance purposes, ensuring all ban/unban actions are permanently logged. The unban action does not delete the ban record but marks it as inactive.

Related operations:
- GET /user-bans: Retrieve list of all active user bans
- GET /user-bans/{id}: Retrieve specific user ban details
- PATCH /user-bans/{id}/ban: Apply new ban to user
operations.name: unban
operations.specification: Update ecommerce_mall_user_bans table to set is_active = false and update unban_at to current timestamp for the specified user_ban_id. Verify requesting admin has valid admin role (regular or super grade) before proceeding. Preserve complete ban history record with all existing fields. Return updated ban record with new is_active = false status.

responseBody.description: Updated user ban record with is_active = false

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user ban record to unban
parameters.name: userBanId

operations.description:
Create a seller suspension record to disable a seller's account privileges.

This operation allows administrators to suspend a seller's account, which triggers several system behaviors:

- The seller's approval status is set to suspended
- All products created by the seller are hidden from search results and category listings
- The seller is prevented from creating new products or editing existing products
- The seller can continue processing existing orders (shipping, responding to cancellation and refund requests)

The suspension record captures:

- The seller being suspended
- The administrator who performed the suspension
- An optional reason for the suspension
- The timestamp when the suspension was created

To reinstate a suspended seller, use the PATCH /seller-suspensions/:id/unsuspend operation.

**Security Considerations:**

This operation is restricted to administrators only. Regular sellers and customers cannot create suspension records. The system automatically associates the current authenticated administrator's ID with the suspension record.

**Relationship to Other Operations:**

- GET /admin/sellers/:id/suspensions - Retrieve suspension history for a specific seller
- PATCH /seller-suspensions/:id/unsuspend - Reinstates a suspended seller
operations.name: suspend
operations.specification:
Create a new seller_suspensions record with the current authenticated admin's ID.

Database operation:

1. Extract admin_id from authenticated session context
2. Extract seller_id from request body
3. Extract optional reason from request body
4. Create ecommerce_mall_seller_suspensions record with:
   - seller_id = from request
   - admin_id = from authenticated session
   - reason = from request (nullable)
   - created_at = current timestamp
   - updated_at = current timestamp
   - deleted_at = null
   - reinstated_at = null
   - reinstated_by_id = null

Return created record with 201 status code.

responseBody.description: Created seller suspension record

requestBody.description: Seller suspension creation request

operations.description:
Reinstate a previously suspended seller account.

This operation permanently reinstates a seller account that was previously suspended by administrators. The operation updates the seller suspension record by setting the reinstitution timestamp and administrator who performed the action. After unsuspension, the seller regains full platform access including ability to create and edit products, while their existing products remain available in search and category listings. The operation preserves the complete audit trail of the suspension lifecycle in the `ecommerce_mall_seller_suspensions` table.

Security considerations: Only authenticated administrators with regular or super grade can perform this operation. The system verifies the requesting admin's role and grade before allowing the reinstitution. This operation does not affect the seller's account status or approval status directly - it only manages the suspension record for audit and business rule enforcement purposes.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the seller suspension record to reinstate.
parameters.name: sellerSuspensionId

requestBody.description: Request body for unsuspend operation - currently empty as the reinstitution is implicit based on the action.

responseBody.description: The updated seller suspension record showing the reinstitution timestamp and administrator.

operations.specification: Update the seller suspension record by setting `reinstated_at` to the current timestamp and `reinstated_by_id` to the authenticated admin's ID. The operation must verify that the requesting user has admin permissions (regular or super grade). Update only the specific seller suspension record by `id` using a single SQL UPDATE statement. The operation is idempotent - if the seller is already reinstated, the system should handle gracefully. After successful reinstitution, the seller's suspension is effectively ended and they regain full platform capabilities.

operations.description:
Create a product deletion request for administrator-initiated product removal due to policy violations.

This endpoint allows administrators to formally request the deletion of a product for policy violations, initiating a review workflow. When an administrator identifies a product that violates platform policies, they can submit a deletion request with detailed reasoning. The request enters a pending status and can be approved or rejected by authorized administrators.

The product deletion process is carefully designed to preserve audit trail and maintain data integrity:
- Product snapshots are preserved to maintain historical record of product information
- Order snapshots are preserved to maintain order history
- The original product is marked as deleted but remains in the system for audit purposes
- All deletion requests are logged with timestamps and responsible administrators

The system enforces strict validation:
- Only administrators with appropriate privileges can submit deletion requests
- Product must exist and be available for deletion
- Deletion request must include a valid reason
- The deletion process follows a workflow that preserves business data integrity
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new product deletion request record in the ecommerce_mall_product_deletions table.
1. Validate that the current user is an administrator
2. Validate that the product_id references an existing product
3. Validate that the reason field is not empty
4. Create the deletion request with status 'pending'
5. Set the admin_id to the current administrator's ID
6. Return the created record with all timestamps

responseBody.description: The created product deletion request record

requestBody.description: Product deletion request information including the product to delete and reason for deletion

operations.description:
Search and filter products with comprehensive search and browsing capabilities.

This operation provides advanced product search functionality allowing customers to search by product name, filter by category (including subcategories), filter by price range (minimum and maximum), filter for in-stock products only, and sort by various criteria. The search results follow the product search and listing expectations defined in the business requirements, ensuring consistent browsing experience across the platform.

## Search Capabilities
- Keyword search by product name
- Category filtering with automatic subcategory inclusion
- Price range filtering (minimum and maximum)
- In-stock only filtering
- Multiple sort options: newest, price ascending, price descending

## Filtering Details
- Category filtering includes products from both parent and child categories
- In-stock filtering excludes products where all variants have zero stock
- Products from suspended sellers are excluded regardless of filter combination

## Response Information
- Products displayed with main image thumbnail, name, seller shop name, base price or price range, and average rating
- Products with no variants are marked as unavailable
- Out-of-stock variants are indicated in listings

## Error Handling
- Empty search terms return no results unless combined with filters
- Deleted products are excluded from search results
- Invalid category references are handled gracefully
operations.name: search
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_products table with pagination and comprehensive filtering.
Join with ecommerce_mall_product_variants for stock quantity and price information.
Apply category filter including subcategories using hierarchical category query.
Apply price range filtering on product base_price.
Apply in_stock filter excluding products where all variants have zero stock.
Apply search filters on product name using case-insensitive matching.
Join with ecommerce_mall_sellers to exclude suspended sellers.
Support pagination with configurable page size (default 20 items per page).
Support sorting by newest (created_at DESC), price_asc (base_price ASC), price_desc (base_price DESC).
Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets.
Optimize queries with existing indexes on created_at, base_price, is_available, seller_id, and name (gin_trgm_ops).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product summaries with key information for browsing

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve product performance analytics and statistics.

This operation provides comprehensive performance metrics for products including sales volume, revenue generation, customer engagement, and review-based insights. It enables sellers and administrators to analyze how products are performing across the marketplace.

The analytics endpoint supports complex filtering to analyze specific product segments, time ranges, or performance thresholds. All metrics are aggregated from the underlying order items, product snapshots, and review data to provide actionable business insights.

Key features include:
- Sales performance metrics: total units sold, revenue generated, order counts
- Customer engagement metrics: view counts, wishlist additions, cart additions
- Review analytics: average ratings, review counts, positive/negative sentiment
- Time-based filtering: date ranges for performance analysis
- Category and seller filtering: segment analysis by category or seller
- Inventory status: current stock levels and availability impact on sales
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_products and ecommerce_mall_order_items tables to calculate aggregated product performance metrics.

Join products with order_items to calculate sales metrics (total_quantity, total_revenue).
Join products with reviews to calculate review metrics (average_rating, review_count).
Filter by optional criteria: seller_id, category_id, date range (created_at, updated_at), minimum/maximum sales, inventory thresholds.
Apply pagination to return subset of products with analytics.
Return paginated list of product performance summaries including: product info, sales metrics, engagement metrics, review metrics, inventory status.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product performance summaries with aggregated metrics

requestBody.description: Analytics search criteria and filtering parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated customer behavior analytics for insights and trend analysis.

This operation provides comprehensive analytics on customer shopping patterns, including product views, cart additions, checkout behavior, and purchase trends. The analytics are designed for sellers to understand their customer base and for administrators to monitor platform-wide engagement metrics.

The operation supports advanced filtering capabilities to segment customer behavior by product categories, price ranges, time periods, and customer segments. It aggregates data across all customer interactions including product views, wishlist additions, cart contents, order placements, and review activities.

The system preserves customer privacy by returning only aggregated metrics without exposing individual customer data. All analytics are computed from anonymized session data to ensure compliance with privacy regulations.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query aggregated customer behavior metrics from analytics tables.
Filter by product categories, time periods, and customer segments.
Calculate metrics: product views, cart additions, conversion rates, average order value.
Support pagination, sorting by metric value, and date range filtering.
Aggregate data across customer sessions and purchase history.
Return summarized metrics for dashboard displays and trend analysis.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of customer behavior analytics summaries

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring

ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once

activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.

credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
